correctness.rationale: For any calibrated boundary \(g\), defining \(K=\sup g(s)/(z_\alpha\sqrt{s})\) gives the pointwise envelope \(g(s)\le K z_\alpha\sqrt{s}\). Event inclusion then forces \(K z_\alpha\) to be at least the \(1-\alpha\) quantile of \(\sup |W(s)|/\sqrt{s}\), and the square-root boundary attains equality. The mean-width normalization was checked against Theorem 3.3 of arXiv:2608.03889v1.

value.rationale: The theorem turns a practically interpretable precision objective—minimizing the largest multiplicative width penalty versus ordinary fixed-time Gaussian intervals—into an exact global design rule. It elevates the q=1/2 square-root/Pocock shape from one option in a parametric family to an optimizer over all deterministic Brownian boundary shapes for this loss, while explicitly separating this criterion from power and stopping-time goals.
